Welcome, and thank you for signing up to test MailCraft.

**Getting started**
- Install the [latest release](https://github.com/billsecond/mailcraft/releases/latest). The builds aren't signed yet, so Windows and macOS will warn you the first time you open them.
- For a work or school account, your organisation may need to approve MailCraft once ("Need admin approval"). MailCraft says what to do: open Microsoft's approval page if you're an administrator, or copy a message for one.
- Keep Outlook or Outlook on the web to hand. Moves, deletions and read marks go to your server, and alpha builds can get things wrong.

**Reporting**
- One problem per issue, through the [problem form](https://github.com/billsecond/mailcraft/issues/new?template=problem.yml). Mention this issue so it's linked to you.
- Say which version you're on (File › About MailCraft) and whether it lost anything, crashed, or disagrees with Outlook on the web. Those get the `data-loss`, `crash` and `out-of-step` labels and are fixed first.
- From the release after 0.3.0, paste **Help › Copy Diagnostics** into the report: it has the version, the platform and the end of the log, with addresses, names and paths taken out.
- Put nothing private in an issue: no message content, addresses or organisation names.

**This issue is your log.** A short comment once a week is plenty: which devices you used, roughly how many days, and anything odd that didn't merit its own issue.

**The beta** counts 14 working days (Monday to Friday, about three weeks) on at least 2 devices. When it starts, we'll ask here, and your 14 working days begin then. Nothing in the alpha counts towards it, so use it as much or as little as you like for now.

New releases are announced in #11. **Watch → Custom → Releases** on the repository gets you a notification.

Thanks again! A maintainer will add you to the roster in #11.

<sub>This reply is posted automatically for every tester sign-up.</sub>
